methodological_rigor.justification: The authors benchmark HRCHY-CytoCommunity against NeST and six non-hierarchical methods (CellCharter, NicheCompass, GraphST, SpaGCN, SpaSEG, Giotto Suite) across eight diverse spatial omics datasets (CODEX, MERFISH, Stereo-seq, Visium HD, Slide-seq V2, Visium V1, MIBI-TOF, IMC), using ground-truth annotations from original studies. They include comprehensive ablations, sensitivity analyses (DropNode rate, lambda_consis, lambda_balance, K, M), robustness tests against label noise, and scalability assessments (up to 473k spots). Statistical testing uses one-sided paired t-tests on AMI/Macro-F1, hypergeometric and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, tumor grade, and tumor size. Minor gaps include reliance on one-sided tests, no multiplicity correction across the many benchmark comparisons, and survival analyses that are exploratory within selected subgroups (e.g., 29 and 13 patient subgroups) without pre-registration or independent validation cohort.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The framework is applied to a 263-patient breast cancer IMC cohort with 73 deaths, producing hierarchical prognostic stratification (TC-13 HR=0.20 p=0.031; CN-21 HR=2.2 p=0.026; CN-34 HR=5.4 p<0.001), and demonstrates that fine-grained CN analysis uncovers patient heterogeneity not explained by cell-type abundance alone. However, all clinical analyses are retrospective on previously published cohorts with no prospective or external validation, and subgroup analyses are exploratory within a single Group 1 partition. The work is primarily a computational methods contribution; clinical utility is illustrative rather than practice-changing, placing it in the plausible-translational-implications tier and consistent with Oxford LoE 4 (retrospective/case-series-like analysis of existing datasets).

reporting_quality.justification: As a computational methods paper, no single clinical reporting checklist applies cleanly; the manuscript references a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary and reports methods, datasets (Supplementary Data 1), hyperparameters (Supplementary Table 1 and 2), loss functions, and evaluation metrics with equations. Code is deposited on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.18137898) with Source Data files provided for each figure, and eight Supplementary Notes cover ablation, sensitivity, robustness, scalability, and platform-exclusion rationale. URLs to tutorials and repositories are redacted in the provided text but are cited. Omissions include no formal TRIPOD-style model card for the prognostic application and limited prospective-reporting detail on the survival sub-analyses.

novelty_literature.justification: HRCHY-CytoCommunity is positioned as a hierarchical extension of the authors' prior CytoCommunity framework and addresses explicit gaps in NeST (incomplete cellular coverage, non-nested assignments, reliance on gene-expression hotspots, fragmentation of spatially discontinuous structures). The combination of differentiable graph pooling, adaptive edge pruning, consistency and balance regularization (GRAND-inspired DropNode), and adaptive alpha scheduling within a unified end-to-end hierarchical objective is a meaningful methodological contribution rather than an incremental tweak. Novelty is bounded because each individual component (MinCut loss, DiffPool, GRAND, DropNode) is drawn from existing literature, and the biological findings (CK7+ favorable prognosis, CAF fence-like structures, TLS-like B/T co-enrichment) largely recapitulate known associations rather than discovering new biology.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear problem statement, methods-then-results flow, and effective use of six main figures plus extensive supplementary material. Concepts are introduced progressively (base module, regularization module, cross-sample alignment, clinical application), and figure legends are detailed with explicit statistical annotations. Some passages are dense with inline LaTeX math fragments that would benefit from cleaner typesetting, and a few paragraphs in Results are lengthy and could be tightened, but overall clarity is strong and publication-ready.

key_strengths: Unified end-to-end hierarchical GNN with differentiable pooling, adaptive edge pruning, and consistency/balance regularization producing fully nested assignments with complete cellular coverage
Broad benchmarking against NeST and six non-hierarchical methods across eight datasets spanning CODEX, MERFISH, Stereo-seq, Visium HD, Slide-seq V2, Visium V1, MIBI-TOF, and IMC modalities
Extensive ablation, sensitivity, robustness (label-noise), and scalability analyses (473k spots in 8.02 min, 8.69 GB)
Clinically-oriented application on 263-patient IMC breast cancer cohort with multivariable Cox regression adjusting for age, grade, and tumor size, yielding interpretable TC/CN prognostic subgroups
Open code on Zenodo and Source Data files supporting each main figure
key_concerns: Prognostic findings (TC-13, CN-21, CN-34) are derived from exploratory subgroup analyses within a single retrospective cohort with no external validation and small event counts (34 events in Group 1 analyses)
Statistical comparisons rely on one-sided paired t-tests without multiplicity correction across the many method/dataset combinations
Method-selection exclusions (e.g., GraphST/Giotto/SpaSEG excluded on certain datasets for memory or applicability reasons) could bias head-to-head benchmarking
Biological findings in the clinical application largely recapitulate known associations (CK7+, CAF barriers, TLS-like structures) rather than uncovering novel biology
Optimal (c1, c2) selection partially fixes known ground-truth values on datasets where annotations exist, which may inflate apparent performance
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid computational-methods paper with rigorous benchmarking, strong engineering contribution, and a retrospective but credibly executed translational application; fits Tier 2 (e.g., Nature Communications / Genome Biology-class venues) with minor revisions to tighten statistical reporting and temper clinical claims.
